glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.intro: The words {{brand}} uses, and how they relate.
glossary.relation: A service consists of applications. An application runs on systems. {{brand}} reaches systems and applications through platforms.

service.text: What a team offers to others, with an owner and a criticality. It consists of applications.

application.text: Software a service consists of, with a CIA rating. It runs on systems.

system.text: Where applications run: a server, VM, cluster, appliance or cloud service, with its environments. Part of the catalogue.

component.text: A code or data part of an application: a repository, image, library, topic or database.

platform.text: A connection {{brand}} talks to through an API: base URL, credentials, API specifications. Not a catalogue entry.

process.text: A versioned flow of steps that {{brand}} runs. “Procedure” and “runbook” mean the same thing in these docs.

run.text: One execution of a process, with its journal and evidence.

step.text: One node of a process in a run: a call, a check, a manual task or a decision.

decision.text: An approval or selection a person makes while a run waits (My tasks).

monitor.text: A graph of checks that runs on a schedule and reports a status.

check.text: One test inside a monitor or a process step (e.g. HTTP status, a query value).

objective.text: An availability target of a service, measured over time (the scorecard).

document.text: A record with a type and a workflow: change requests, decisions, reviews, firewall changes. In the docs also called a record.

credential.text: Metadata about secrets kept elsewhere (expiry, rotation, owner). It never holds the secret itself; platforms do.

duty.text: A recurring obligation of a service, judged by real runs: done, late or missed.

team.text: A team groups people with roles. The owning teams of an item decide who may see and change it.

module.text: An optional area an administrator can switch off in Settings → Modules.

notYours.title: You do not use this module
notYours.text: Ask an administrator if you need it.

access.title: Who may use {{name}}
access.intro: Everyone signed in uses a module by default. Restricted to selected teams and users, it is left out for everyone else – its pages, menu entries, notifications and report sections. Administrators and auditors always use every module.

modeHint.everyone: The default: everyone who may sign in to {{brand}}.
modeHint.selected: Only the teams and users below (a team: its members). A single sign-on group reaches the module through the team it is mapped to.

access.subjectsHint: Teams are kept up to date by their members and by the single sign-on team mapping (Users → Teams).
access.unknownHint: A deleted team stays on the list and matches nobody, so deleting a team never opens the module.

now.everyone: Now: everyone signed in uses this module.

access.previewing: Working out who gains and who loses the module…
access.previewFailed: Could not work out who gains and who loses the module. Try again.
access.nobodyChanges: Nobody gains or loses the module.
access.owningTeamsWithout: These teams own items of the module but would not use it: {{teams}}. Their members keep the items' rights but cannot open them.
access.widensHint: This widens who uses the module: saving asks you to confirm that it is you.
access.confirmLoses_one: {{count}} person loses the module. Their notifications and report sections of it stop at once.
access.confirmLoses_other: {{count}} people lose the module. Their notifications and report sections of it stop at once.
access.confirmNobody: Nobody loses the module now, but the list gets shorter.
access.notSaved: Who may use the module was not saved
access.rolesIntro: {{name}} has module roles: viewer, contributor and manager. Core roles give one by default (a designer is a manager, an operator a contributor, a viewer a viewer); a role given here adds – the highest counts. A team’s role applies to its members across the whole module.
access.roleDefaultHint: Uses it, with the role their core roles give
access.everyoneRolesHint: Open to everyone, only entries with a module role are kept.
